title: Octopus has three hearts
hook: An octopus has three hearts, and blue blood.

scenes.narration: An octopus has three hearts.
Two of them pump blood through the gills.
The third pumps blood around the rest of the body.
Its blood is blue, because it carries oxygen using copper instead of iron.
When an octopus swims, the main heart actually stops beating.
That is why octopuses prefer crawling. Follow for more facts.

script.caption: Three hearts, blue blood, and a heart that stops when it swims. Octopuses are wild.
fact_check: Blood is blue due to copper-based hemocyanin

title: Honey never spoils
hook: Honey can last for thousands of years.

scenes.narration: Honey can last for thousands of years.
Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs.
It was still safe to eat after about three thousand years.
Honey has very little water, so bacteria cannot grow in it.
It is also acidic, and bees add an enzyme that makes a little hydrogen peroxide.
So honey is nearly impossible to spoil. Follow for more.

script.caption: The one food that basically never expires.
fact_check: Edible honey reported in ancient Egyptian tombs
Low water content and acidity inhibit microbes

title: A day on Venus is longer than its year
hook: On Venus, a day is longer than a year.

scenes.narration: On Venus, a day lasts longer than a year.
Venus spins very slowly, taking about 243 Earth days to turn once.
But it circles the Sun in only about 225 Earth days.
So one Venus year is shorter than one Venus day.
And Venus spins backwards compared to most planets.
Strange world next door. Follow for more space facts.

script.caption: Venus is the only planet where the day outlasts the year.
fact_check: Venus sidereal rotation about 243 Earth days
Venus orbital period about 225 Earth days

title: Bananas are berries
hook: Botanically, a banana is a berry. A strawberry is not.

scenes.narration: Botanically, a banana is a berry.
A strawberry is not.
To a botanist, a berry grows from one flower with one ovary, and has seeds inside the flesh.
Bananas fit that definition. So do grapes, tomatoes and even watermelons.
Strawberries do not, because their seeds sit on the outside.
Nature ignores the grocery store. Follow for more.

script.caption: Science defines berries differently than your kitchen does.
fact_check: Strawberry is an aggregate accessory fruit, not a true berry
Grapes and tomatoes are botanical berries

title: Lightning is hotter than the Sun
hook: A lightning bolt is hotter than the surface of the Sun.

scenes.narration: A lightning bolt is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
The Sun's surface is about five thousand five hundred degrees Celsius.
The air in a lightning channel can reach around thirty thousand degrees.
That is roughly five times hotter.
The air expands so fast that it creates a shock wave. That is thunder.
Hot, loud and quick. Follow for more.

script.caption: Lightning heats the air hotter than the Sun's surface, for a split second.
fact_check: Lightning channel up to about 30,000 K
Thunder is a shock wave from rapid air expansion

title: Wombats make cube-shaped poop
hook: Wombats are the only animals that make cube-shaped poop.

scenes.narration: Wombats make cube-shaped poop.
They are the only known animal that does this.
Researchers found that parts of the wombat's intestine are stretchy and some parts are stiff.
That uneven squeezing shapes the waste into cubes.
Cubes do not roll away, so wombats stack them to mark territory.
Nature is weird. Follow for more.

script.caption: Why the cube? Uneven intestines, and a very good reason.
fact_check: Intestinal elasticity varies along the intestine

scenes.narration: Sharks are older than trees.
The first sharks appeared more than four hundred million years ago.
The earliest trees showed up around three hundred and eighty million years ago.
So sharks were swimming for tens of millions of years before any forest existed.
They have survived several mass extinctions since.
Ancient survivors. Follow for more.

script.caption: Sharks were here before the first forest.
fact_check: Earliest shark fossils around 400+ million years old
Earliest trees (e.g. Archaeopteris/Wattieza) about 385-370 million years ago

title: Cleopatra and the Moon landing
hook: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

scenes.narration: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
The Great Pyramid was built around twenty five hundred BC.
Cleopatra was born in sixty nine BC.
That is about twenty five centuries after the pyramid.
The Moon landing was in nineteen sixty nine, only about two thousand years after her.
History is longer than it feels. Follow for more.

script.caption: Deep time is hard to imagine.

title: Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire
hook: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.

scenes.narration: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
Teaching was already happening at Oxford in ten ninety six.
The Aztec capital, Tenochtitlan, was founded in thirteen twenty five.
That is more than two centuries later.
Oxford was already old when the Aztecs began to build their city.
History overlaps in surprising ways. Follow for more.

script.caption: Dates make history stranger than fiction.

title: Days used to be shorter
hook: When dinosaurs lived, a day was shorter than 24 hours.

scenes.narration: When dinosaurs lived, a day was shorter than twenty four hours.
Around seventy million years ago, a day lasted about twenty three and a half hours.
The Moon is the reason this changes.
Its gravity creates ocean tides, and tidal friction slowly drags on Earth's spin.
The days get longer by about two milliseconds each century.
Time is slowly stretching. Follow for more.

script.caption: Our days are getting longer, very slowly.
fact_check: Day length ~23.5 h about 70 million years ago
